meta.label: IgA nephropathy patient journey
notes: Chronological clinical arc for primary IgA nephropathy (IgAN), anchored to moments patients describe rather than the chapters clinicians use.

Reflects the 2021-25 landscape shift: RAASi + SGLT2i as supportive backbone, with targeted-release budesonide (Tarpeyo), sparsentan (Filspari), iptacopan (Fabhalta), and atrasentan (Vanrafia) added as escalation lanes.

Trial-consideration / in-trial stages weighted toward the active APRIL / BLyS / complement-pathway pipeline (sibeprenlimab VISIONARY, atacicept ORIGIN, povetacicept RAINIER, BHV-1400, etc.) — that is the corpus we have.
Adapted from the lupus_nephritis journey; the two share a nephrology spine but the IgAN treatment ladder and trial landscape are distinct.

stages.label: Pre-diagnosis
stages.description: Before IgAN is named. Often an incidental finding — visible hematuria during a URI, foamy urine, edema, high blood pressure on a routine visit, or microscopic hematuria + proteinuria flagged on an exam urinalysis.

steps.label: Symptom onset
steps.description: First noticing something is wrong: synpharyngitic gross hematuria, foamy urine, swelling, fatigue, or high blood pressure.

steps.label: Incidental finding
steps.description: Hematuria or proteinuria caught on a routine / pre-employment / military / pregnancy urinalysis with no symptoms reported.

steps.label: Pre-diagnosis uncertainty
steps.description: Waiting on referral and repeat labs, not knowing whether this is transient, infectious, or something kidney-specific.

stages.label: Diagnostic odyssey
stages.description: PCP → nephrology referral, repeat urinalysis + UPCR / 24-hr protein + serum creatinine + eGFR; ANA/dsDNA / complement to rule out lupus; ultimately kidney biopsy with Oxford MEST-C grading to confirm IgAN and stage it.

steps.label: Nephrology referral
steps.description: First nephrologist visit; the workup conversation about repeat protein quantification, kidney imaging, and the biopsy threshold.

steps.label: Biopsy and MEST-C grading
steps.description: Native kidney biopsy and the moment of receiving the Oxford MEST-C score (M, E, S, T, C) that anchors prognosis and treatment intensity.

steps.label: Diagnosis named
steps.description: The moment IgA nephropathy is confirmed as the diagnosis; first conversations about prognosis, life-expectancy framing, and the long progression curve.

stages.label: Supportive baseline
stages.description: Baseline disease-modifying regimen: maximally-tolerated ACEi/ARB (RAASi) plus SGLT2 inhibitor (dapagliflozin / empagliflozin), low-salt diet, blood-pressure control, and dietary protein adjustment. The foundation every IgAN patient stays on.

steps.label: RAASi titration
steps.description: Starting and titrating ACEi or ARB to maximum tolerated dose; learning to track home BP and serum creatinine after dose changes.

steps.label: SGLT2i started
steps.description: Adding an SGLT2 inhibitor (Farxiga / Jardiance); navigating glucosuria, UTI risk, and the off-label-to-on-label shift in payer coverage.

steps.label: Lifestyle adjustments
steps.description: Salt, protein, and fluid changes; hypertension self-management; weight, alcohol, and exercise tuning around eGFR.

stages.label: Treatment escalation
stages.description: Persistent proteinuria above goal despite supportive care triggers escalation: targeted-release budesonide (Tarpeyo / Nefecon), sparsentan (Filspari), atrasentan (Vanrafia), or iptacopan (Fabhalta). Often layered, often switched.

steps.label: Starting targeted therapy
steps.description: First weeks on Tarpeyo / Filspari / Vanrafia / Fabhalta; the prior-auth / specialty-pharmacy / cost-of-therapy onboarding.

steps.label: Side effects and tolerability
steps.description: Steroid-like effects from budesonide-ER, edema and LFT monitoring from endothelin antagonists, vaccination requirements for complement inhibitors.

steps.label: Response monitoring
steps.description: Watching UPCR / 24-hr proteinuria, eGFR slope, and BP at 3 / 6 / 9-month checkpoints; deciding whether to continue, layer, or switch.

steps.label: Drug switching
steps.description: Cycling between targeted therapies after partial response or intolerance; the hope-then-disappointment loop that defines this stage.

stages.label: Stable management
stages.description: Proteinuria suppressed at or near target with the current regimen; eGFR holding. Long-term follow-up cadence, infection precautions for those on immunosuppression, life adjusted around the regimen.

steps.label: Long-term regimen
steps.description: Daily medication routine settled; quarterly labs; nephrology visits every 3-6 months.

steps.label: Infection and vaccine routine
steps.description: Annual flu, COVID, pneumococcal, and meningococcal vaccination (especially for complement-inhibitor patients); avoidance practices.

steps.label: Identity with chronic disease
steps.description: Adjusting to a chronic-but-managed framing; navigating career, family planning, and life choices around CKD stage.

stages.label: Progression
stages.description: Despite treatment, eGFR continues to decline and CKD stage advances. Conversations shift to slowing the slope, dialysis planning, transplant evaluation, and the emotional cost of a progressive disease.

steps.label: eGFR decline
steps.description: Recognising a sustained downward slope on eGFR despite max-tolerated therapy; the conversation about what stops working when.

steps.label: Advancing CKD stage
steps.description: Crossing into Stage 3b, 4, or 5; the symptom changes (fatigue, anemia, mineral-bone, appetite) and lab additions that mark each step.

steps.label: Transplant evaluation
steps.description: Referral to transplant clinic, donor conversations with family, financial and insurance workup, getting onto the deceased-donor list.

steps.label: Dialysis preparation
steps.description: Vascular access (fistula), modality choice (HD vs PD), training, and the lived adjustment to a dialysis schedule.

stages.label: Trial consideration
stages.description: Exploring the APRIL / BLyS / complement-pathway pipeline — sibeprenlimab (VISIONARY), atacicept (ORIGIN), povetacicept (RAINIER), BHV-1400, zigakibart, and others. Reading the late-phase data, talking to community, working out eligibility, weighing logistical / financial / personal cost.

steps.label: Trial awareness
steps.description: Hearing about a late-phase IgAN trial (sibeprenlimab, atacicept, povetacicept, BHV-1400, etc.) through community, advocacy, ClinicalTrials.gov, or clinician; initial reading of the readouts.

steps.label: Eligibility self-assessment
steps.description: Working out whether eGFR, proteinuria, prior therapies, biopsy timing, and geography qualify for a given trial; trial-by-trial matrix-building.

steps.label: Logistical assessment
steps.description: Travel to site, time off work, caregiver availability, copay / insurance / drug-cost while in trial, and the every-4-weeks infusion / injection cadence.

steps.label: Consent or decline
steps.description: The decision moment — sign on, defer, or decline. Often shaped by family situation, payer coverage of standard-of-care during the trial, and risk tolerance for placebo arms.

stages.label: In-trial experience
stages.description: Active trial participation. The dosing visits (every 4 weeks for most APRIL / BLyS biologics), the protocol labs, the open-label-extension question, and the cycle of week-by-week proteinuria / UPCR updates that becomes the rhythm of life.

steps.label: Screening and consent
steps.description: Site visit, screening labs and biopsy review, informed consent, and the wait between screening and randomization.

steps.label: Active dosing
steps.description: On-trial dosing rhythm (often Q4W); the lived experience of being on what may be drug or placebo and tracking symptoms / labs against trial expectations.

steps.label: Side effects and safety
steps.description: Trial-related adverse events, infections, immunoglobulin / complement monitoring, and infusion / injection reactions.

steps.label: Interim readouts
steps.description: Public interim or topline announcements (e.g. VISIONARY interim, ORIGIN-3 readout) and the community / personal interpretation of what it means for one's own trial arm.

stages.label: Post-trial
stages.description: After the active treatment phase. Open-label extension, transition back to standard of care, FDA approval and commercial access, or — when the drug fails to show benefit — adjusting expectations and moving to the next option.

steps.label: Open-label extension
steps.description: Rolling into the OLE arm to ensure access to active drug; the new schedule and the longer-term safety conversation.

steps.label: Transition to commercial
steps.description: FDA approval, payer / formulary navigation, and moving from free trial supply to insured access — copay, prior-auth, and bridge programs.

steps.label: Long-term follow-up
steps.description: Years-out monitoring for durability, delayed adverse effects, immunoglobulin / vaccine response, and the question of whether disease has been quieted or merely deferred.
